title: Counter and defaultdict
summary: The collections module's counting and grouping tools, and when they beat a plain dict.
hints: `letter_counts`: `Counter(ch for ch in text.lower() if ch.isalpha())`. A `Counter` is a dict subclass, so returning it is fine. `most_common_word`: `Counter(text.lower().split()).most_common(1)` returns a list with one `(word, count)` pair; ties keep first-seen order.

`is_anagram`: compare two Counters of the letters, ignoring spaces and case: `Counter(a.lower().replace(" ", "")) == Counter(...)`. `combine`: start with an empty `Counter()` and call `.update(d)` for each dict; return `dict(total)`.

`index_words`: `index = defaultdict(list)`, then for `line_no, line in enumerate(lines, start=1)` and each distinct word in that line (`dict.fromkeys(line.lower().split())` keeps order and drops repeats), `index[word].append(line_no)`. Return `dict(index)`.
